description: IPSL-CM6-ESMCO2 is an Earth system model developed at the Institut Pierre-Simon Laplace (IPSL), building on the IPSL-CM6A-LR climate model used for CMIP6 (Boucher et al., 2020). It simulates the physical climate system together with an interactive global carbon cycle for CO2, and can be run either with prescribed atmospheric CO2 concentrations (concentration-driven) or with prescribed CO2 emissions (emission-driven), in which case atmospheric CO2 evolves as a result of exchanges with the land and the ocean.  Five components are dynamically simulated. The atmosphere is simulated by LMDZ6.5 on a longitude-latitude grid of 144 x 143 points (about 2.5° x 1.3°) with 79 vertical levels. The land surface model ORCHIDEE v2, embedded in the atmosphere, computes the surface energy, water and carbon budgets, with land heterogeneity described by 15 plant functional types. The ocean is simulated by NEMO v3.6 in the eORCA1 configuration (nominal 1° resolution) with 75 vertical levels. The sea ice model LIM3 and the marine biogeochemistry model PISCES v2, which represents the lower trophic levels of the marine ecosystem and the cycles of carbon and the main nutrients, run within NEMO on the ocean grid. The atmosphere and the ocean exchange energy, water, momentum and carbon through a coupler.  Three components are prescribed rather than simulated: aerosols, atmospheric chemistry and land ice.
